correctness.rationale: An independent spectral upper bound uses an embedding with hub at zero. The other n−1 clique vertices have a regular simplex of side one in an orthogonal plane or subspace, of squared circumradius (n−2)/(2(n−1)), translated along an axis to height S_n/(n−1) so every hub edge has length one. Their resultant is S_n along the axis. If m<S_n, put all pendant vertices at the opposite axial unit vector. Otherwise use unit vectors with common axial coordinate −S_n/m and transverse components summing to zero; m>=2 permits this, and the equality case has zero transverse component. All graph edge lengths are at most one, and the centered sum of squared norms is D_{n,m}. Applying the Rayleigh inequality to each centered coordinate gives lambda_2*D_{n,m}<=sum_e w_e times its squared length<=B for every feasible weight vector. For attainability, the two difference spaces have eigenvalues c and a+(n−1)b; the nonzero quotient roots have sum na+(m+1)c and product (n+m)ac. Substitution of the stated active weights gives one quotient root equal to 1, the other greater than 1, and the difference-space constraints, with exact cost D_{n,m}. At and above equality the stated uniform star has unit target gap. If m>=S_n, equality in the embedding bound forces its nonzero centered axial coordinate vector to be a lambda_2 eigenvector. At each non-hub clique vertex, interior clique terms cancel (same axial value); at each leaf there is one term. Because all these axial entries are nonzero and the centered hub entry is zero, every hub edge has weight lambda_2, consuming the budget and forcing the claimed zero weights, including at m=S_n. If m<S_n, omitting all interior clique edges reduces to a star, whose best gap is B/(n+m−1) by averaging, strictly below the optimum. The exhibited active design has every edge positive.
residual_risks: Replay independently checks the symbolic active cost and quotient polynomial at 1 only; it does not constitute an all-allocations certificate. That bound and the support statement follow analytically.

evidence: The separator-shadow paper derives ray placement for nonheavy pieces of an articulation splitting and hub centering when the articulation is central in the graph-distance sum criterion. On the pineapple the piece distances sum to n−1 for the clique and 1 for each leaf, so its sufficient hub-centering criterion covers m>=n−1. Its examples treat a simplex for a standalone clique and a graph with independent vertices adjacent to every clique vertex, not the pineapple threshold.
The general FMMP duality is exact; its §5.1 example is a finite unequal-cost instance with different attachments. Topcu–Sorgun–Haemers study adjacency spectra of the very same pineapple topology.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The sufficient articulation criterion uses distances within components, not the lower feasible resultant S_n imposed by unit clique edge lengths. It does not decide the transition in the range m<n−1 or compute the active conductance budget. Adjacency cospectrality does not address variable-weight Laplacians.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: General variational formulations and ray-placement theorems leave a graph-specific optimization and a nontrivial equality analysis. They do not mechanically give the (S_n−m)_+^2 term, the sharp threshold below n−1 or the support dichotomy across it. The discrete-time SLEM phases cannot substitute for that implication.

evidence: The Sun–Boyd–Xiao–Diaconis geometric dual is the centered Euclidean variance with per-edge distances at most one for equal conductance costs; its optimum is the minimal budget for a unit spectral gap. Göring–Helmberg–Wappler treat the corresponding absolute algebraic connectivity framework.
The discrete-time pineapple article optimizes SLEM and permits holding probabilities; its threshold is r=a in its notation.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The unit-gap budget, absolute algebraic connectivity and equal-length variance dual are equivalent after normalization, so coverage could appear in those forms. The stochastic-matrix SLEM optimum depends also on the top Laplacian eigenvalue and row probability constraints, so the same graph is not enough for equivalence.

value.rationale: A budgeted diffusion on the canonical clique-with-leaves graph can optimally use less of the available topology. The result tells exactly when interior edges go from necessary in any optimum to forbidden in every optimum, and the explicit penalty relative to a star shows the size of the spectral gain in the active regime. The equality and nonsymmetric cases make the cutoff informative beyond finding a symmetric example.
residual_risks: The theorem neither asserts that every interior edge is positive in every active optimizer nor covers costs other than an equal-price budget, one leaf, or discrete-time mixing.
